$comment: Every date/time string a tool accepts — history start_time/end_time, and a DateTime write — and what each runtime must make of it. Driven by BOTH tests/unit/test_datetime_parsing.py and packages/server-node/test/dates.test.mjs, so the grammar is one table rather than two parsers that happen to agree (#157: Node read a zone-less value as the host's local time and Python as UTC, Node accepted '04/23/2026' and 'April 23, 2026' and rolled '2026-02-30' over to March, and Python's own grammar changed between 3.10 and 3.11). `expected` is the instant as ISO-8601 UTC at millisecond precision — the precision a JavaScript Date holds, to which the Python runtime truncates so both send the plant the same instant. `error` is the exact message the value is refused with. The grammar is RFC 3339: date and time both present, seconds and a 1-9 digit fraction optional, 'T', 't' or a space between, and a zone that is 'Z'/'z' or '+HH:MM'/'-HH:MM'. A value with no zone is refused rather than guessed.

cases.name: lower-case z and t, which RFC 3339 allows
an offset shifts the instant rather than being dropped
an offset that moves the UTC date is not an impossible date
a space may separate date and time
microseconds, as the Python runtime returns them, are truncated
OPC UA's own 100ns precision is truncated
truncated, never rounded up into the next second
the first instant OPC UA can carry
an offset can bring a 1600 wall time into range
the last instant OPC UA can carry
no zone: refused, not read as UTC or as local time
cases.error: Invalid date/time: "2026-04-23T17:40:00" has no timezone, so the instant it names depends on where it is read. Add Z for UTC or an offset such as +02:00, e.g. 2026-04-23T17:40:00Z

cases.name: no zone, no seconds
cases.error: Invalid date/time: "2026-04-23T17:40" has no timezone, so the instant it names depends on where it is read. Add Z for UTC or an offset such as +02:00, e.g. 2026-04-23T17:40:00Z

cases.name: no zone, space-separated
cases.error: Invalid date/time: "2026-04-23 17:40:00.123" has no timezone, so the instant it names depends on where it is read. Add Z for UTC or an offset such as +02:00, e.g. 2026-04-23T17:40:00Z

cases.name: a bare year, which Node's Date read as a UTC midnight
ISO basic format, which Python 3.11 read
an ISO week date, which Python 3.11 read
hour 24, which Node's Date rolled into the next day
a leap second, which neither library can hold
30 February, which Node's Date rolled over to 2 March
digits that are not ASCII, which Python's \d matched
before 1601, which an OPC UA DateTime cannot carry
cases.error: Invalid date/time: "1600-12-31T23:59:59Z" is outside what an OPC UA DateTime can hold (1601-01-01T00:00:00Z to 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z)

cases.name: a two-digit-looking year is the year 26, and out of range
cases.error: Invalid date/time: "0026-01-15T00:00:00Z" is outside what an OPC UA DateTime can hold (1601-01-01T00:00:00Z to 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z)

cases.name: the year zero
cases.error: Invalid date/time: "0000-01-01T00:00:00Z" is outside what an OPC UA DateTime can hold (1601-01-01T00:00:00Z to 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z)

cases.name: an offset that carries 9999 into the year 10000
cases.error: Invalid date/time: "9999-12-31T23:59:59-01:00" is outside what an OPC UA DateTime can hold (1601-01-01T00:00:00Z to 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z)
